newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rules out apology to N.Korea over Hunziker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rules out apology to N.Korea over Hunziker.

text.p: The United States on Thursday ruled out an apology to Pyongyang over an American arrested in North Korea, and ridiculed North Korean charges that his religious ignorance proved he was not a missionary but a spy.

The official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said on Thursday that Carl Hunziker, who was arrested Aug. 24, could not be a missionary as he claimed because he did not know the Ten Commandments or how to pray.
It said the situation would only get "gloomier" if the United States did not apologise for the incident and bring South Korea "to task" for employing Hunziker as a spy.
"There's going to be no apology from the United States. We're demanding his release," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
Hunziker's family have said the 26-year-old American was a missionary who crossed into North Korea while on a visit to China. They said he had been working in South Korea before his trip to China.
Burns dismissed KCNA's charges about Hunziker's lack of religious knowledge as "absolutely ludicrous".

KCNA said Hunziker had written and signed a confession that he infiltrated into North Korea in order to spy on "the conditions of the army, the life of civilians, economic conditions and social environment".

But Burns said that when Ake Lafquist, a Swedish diplomat representing American interests in Pyongyang, visited Hunziker last week, the American "told him very clearly" that he had made no such confession.
"The North Koreans are holding an American citizen unjustly. He is innocent. He is a civilian. He has nothing to do with our government," Burns said.

"This young man's motivation for going to North Korea may have been to proselytise, but since we haven't had a lot of contact with him, it's very difficult for us to say exactly what his intentions were," he added.
